land.text: Circassia conquered by Russia: the Kuban, Black Sea coast and Caucasus foothills, ended 21 May 1864

successors.note: The page: 'the Russian Empire's war ended on May 21, 1864'; the Russo-Circassian War page gives June 1864 as the end of the war. Most Circassians were exiled or killed.

capitals.name: Bighuqal (Anapa)
capitals.note: 'Bighuqal (Anapa) was declared the new capital in 1839'; the medieval capital Shanjir has an unknown location. Anapa was in Russian hands from 1829 (Treaty of Adrianople), so this seat was nominal.

capitals.name: Sochi
capitals.note: The parliament was 'established in the capital of Sochi' on 13 June 1860; 'considered by many Circassians as their traditional capital'.

correction.text: 'bounded by the Kuban River on the north which separated it from the Russian Empire', from the Taman Peninsula to Mozdok; 82,000 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1250-1762. Infobox area 82,000 km2; the 12-point fallback polygon (Taman, the south bank of the Kuban to Mozdok, the Caucasus crest and the Black Sea coast) resolves to 70,050 km2 on the gazetteer (ratio 0.85, within a factor of two). No named region fits the whole, so the polygon stands; Kabarda is the Kabardin-Balkar part inside it.

correction.text: Circassia without the Mozdok fort Russia founded in July 1763

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1763-1821: 'It began when the Russian Empire entered Circassia and occupied Mozdok' (July 1763). The page gives no other land change before 1822, and the Kuban line is a siege line, not a border.

correction.text: Circassia without Mozdok and without Kabarda, 'placed under Russian military rule in 1822'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1822-1863. Russia took more of the Black Sea coast after 1830 (slowed after the Circassian victory at Abinsk in 1834) and the Abzakh submitted on 20 November 1859, but the page gives no territory remaining at any date, so the 1822 shape is kept to 1863 (confidence low); the coast and the Kuban plain were already shrinking and need a gap-filler.

ledger.note: c. 1250: Circassia emerges as the land of the Circassian princes. Infobox 'Established: c. 13th century' (the page names Verzacht as 'Grand Prince of Zichia' in 1333 and Inal the Great uniting the principalities between 1427 and 1453); 1250 is the middle of the century and not a dated founding.

region.text: Mozdok, on the eastern edge of Circassia

ledger.note: July 1763: Russia occupies Mozdok and the Russo-Circassian War begins. 'It began when the Russian Empire entered Circassia and occupied Mozdok'; the war ran 'between July 1763 and June 1864'.

region.text: Kabarda (Eastern Circassia), 'placed under Russian military rule in 1822'

ledger.note: 1822: Kabarda passes to Russia. Russo-Circassian War page: 'most Kabardinian princes ultimately submitted to Russian rule and pledged allegiance to the autocracy of the Tsar' (1809-1810), 'The entirety of Kabardia (Eastern Circassia) was then declared property of the Russian government' (1820) and 'The area was placed under Russian military rule in 1822, as Kabardia eventually fully fell'; fighting 'subsided after 1825'; the population fell from 350,000 in 1763 to 37,000 in 1817. The Treaty of Belgrade (1739) had recognised Kabarda's independence (Circassia page). [Repair fx-42, 2 Nov 2026 (dossier request R116): this was an occupation_start with counterpart russian-empire, which the compiler reads as Circassia occupying Russian land (the 47 cells of Kabarda drawn as Russian land hatched with Circassia's colour 1822-1864). Kabarda is Russian land from 1822, as the 1822 keyframe already draws it, so the event is a loss to the Russian Empire. The 1864 occupation_end (old ledger/5) was dropped with it. data/patches/p1820-p1829.json events/2 (occupation_end 1822) now closes nothing.]
1839: Bighuqal (Anapa) is declared the new capital of Circassia ('Hawduqo Mansur: declared leader of the confederation in 1839').

June 1860: the Circassian parliament meets at Sochi. A parliament 'was established in the capital of Sochi on June 13, 1860' with Qerandiqo Berzeg as its head (the war page dates the Circassian Parliament in Sochi 25 June 1861, and Russian General Kolyobakin later destroyed it).

region.text: the last Circassian lands from the Kuban to the Black Sea

ledger.note: 21 May 1864: Russia takes the rest of Circassia. The war ended on that date; 80-97 percent of the Circassians were killed or exiled (the page estimates 600,000-1,500,000 lost; the war page says '1,500,000 were displaced to the Ottoman Empire').

region.text: Circassia, annexed by the Russian Empire

ledger.note: 21 May 1864: Circassia is conquered. The infobox ends the state in 1864; the war ended 'on May 21, 1864'.

wars.name: Russo-Circassian War

zones.text: Circassia from the Kuban to the Black Sea coast and Kabarda

wars.outcome: A hundred-year war: Russia occupied Mozdok (July 1763), put Kabarda under military rule (1822), claimed Circassia by the Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829), landed on the coast in 1838 and crushed the Circassians in the offensive of 1857-1864 (Abzakh submission 20 November 1859; Yevdokimov's campaign from 1862; the war ended 21 May 1864 on the Circassia page, June 1864 on the war page).
wars.note: Ottoman and British aid is claimed for the 1830s; the page does not describe Circassia as an Ottoman vassal.

wars.name: Kabardian refusal of Crimean and Ottoman tribute
wars.outcome: After Ottoman and Crimean tribute demands went unmet in 1708 the Kabardians declared they would never pay again and the Crimean forces were defeated.
wars.note: The Treaty of Belgrade (1739) recognised the independence of Eastern Circassia (Kabarda).

certainty.note: A confederation of tribes: only the Kuban river line and the coast are firm; no page gives any survey line.

notes:
No Cliopatria row (the Russian Empire's Cliopatria shapes cover the Caucasus only to the conquered lines). Circassia is a confederation, not a centralised state, so every border is soft. The 12-point polygon is a fallback (no named region covers the Kuban south bank + Black Sea coast + Kabarda). Start 1250 is the middle of the infobox's 'c. 13th century' and is not a dated event (confidence 1). The long Russian advance (Black Sea Line after 1830, Anapa and the coast, the Abzakh 1859, Yevdokimov 1862-1864) is not drawn because the pages give no territory remaining at any date; a gap-filler should open the Kuban Line, Caucasus Line and Black Sea Coastal Line pages. The Circassia page dates the parliament at Sochi to 13 June 1860 and the war page to 25 June 1861; both are given. The Circassian-held Kabarda (Eastern Circassia) is inside the polygon; the Kabardian principality is not given its own dossier. Needs dossiers elsewhere: russian-empire (counterpart, exists), crimean-khanate (exists). The Dagestani khanates, Abazins, Ubykhs and Karachays are not dossiers here. wikidata null.
Fix pass fx-42 (2 Nov 2026), dossier request R116: ledger/2 (1822) is a loss of Kabarda to russian-empire instead of an occupation_start in the wrong direction, and the 1864 occupation_end that closed it was dropped; the later events moved up one place (the 1864 loss is now ledger/5 and the dissolve ledger/6).
